source: FineWeb CC-MAIN-2024-30, first 2,000 rows of the setup's random 50k sample

sizes.label: Parquet, zstd (level 1, pyarrow default), text column only

note: FineWeb CC-MAIN-2024-30, first 2,000 rows of the setup's random 50k sample; 9 columns (date, dump, file_path, id, language, language_score, text, token_count, url); 1,422,641 tokens with the Qwen3-0.6B tokenizer, vocabulary 151669, so ids need uint32. Sizes are bytes on disk, measured.
reading: zstd shrinks the JSONL 2.8 times; Parquet with zstd is 10% larger than JSONL with zstd only because pyarrow 26 writes zstd at level 1 when no level is given; at level 3 Parquet is 2% smaller (measured by the Storage and loading at scale page), and it lets a reader skip columns. The token shard (5,706,564 bytes) is 2.1 times the zstd JSONL: 4 bytes per token and no compression. A vocabulary of at most 65,536 would allow uint16 and roughly halve it (2,861,282 bytes derived).
loader: A pretraining loader memory-maps the token file (numpy.memmap or Megatron's indexed dataset), so the operating system pages in only the windows a step needs. It draws window start positions with a seeded shuffle (Megatron, datatrove; nanoGPT instead draws random offsets with replacement), gives each data-parallel rank a disjoint slice, and records how many samples it has consumed so a restart resumes at the same place. Measured on these 2,000 documents (median 466 tokens, 90th percentile 1,386): one document per 2,048-token window leaves 67.6% of positions as padding (2,143 windows), packing needs 696 windows at 99.95% fill; at 8,192 tokens the padding share rises to 91.3%. Streaming loaders (MosaicML Streaming, LitData, WebDataset) do the same from object storage, one shard at a time.
